target.title: fix(codex): key turn-abort detection on structural markers not prose
target.body:
## Summary

- Codex app-server abort detection now keys on the stable `<turn_aborted>` structural markers instead of byte-matching crate-internal guidance prose.
- Removes a latent upstream-coupling break: a reworded Codex guidance sentence no longer silently misclassifies aborted turns.

## What Problem This Solves

Addresses #99268 (the prose-coupling half). Deliberately does NOT auto-close: the structured-status classification path noted in review is a separate follow-up.

`isCodexTurnAbortMarkerNotification` classified interrupted turns by comparing the wrapped marker body strictly (`===`) against two full-sentence string literals (`CODEX_INTERRUPTED_USER_GUIDANCE` / `CODEX_INTERRUPTED_DEVELOPER_GUIDANCE`). Those sentences are declared `pub(crate) const` in `codex-rs/core/src/context/turn_aborted.rs` (verified against the pinned `@openai/codex` `0.142.4`) — crate-internal, not protocol surface. Any upstream reword or punctuation change would silently stop the equality match, misclassifying aborted turns with no error or log. This is the same failure class behind repeated abort/terminal-classification fix churn in this harness.

The `<turn_aborted>` tags in the same upstream file are the coarser, durable signal. This change keys detection on those markers alone (a non-empty body wrapped in the tags) and drops the guidance-sentence equality. The existing current-prompt echo guard still prevents false positives from the user prompt being echoed through raw response events.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-turn-watches.test.ts` — 29 passed (6 new, covering canonical guidance, a reworded body, developer role, missing markers, empty body, and prompt-echo guard).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.turn-watches.test.ts` — 66 passed (existing abort/interrupt integration coverage unchanged).
- Did NOT change: the `<turn_aborted>` marker constants themselves, nor the current-prompt echo suppression logic.
